newsitem.title: FRANCE: Societe Generale may sell off more assets.
newsitem.headline: Societe Generale may sell off more assets.

text.p: French bank Societe Generale said on Monday it was considering selling off more of its share and property assets but no decision would be made until next year.
The asset sales could trigger significant capital gains.
"We're at the review stage," a spokesman said. "We're seeing whether we're making optimal use of shareholder funds. This is an exercise we carry out from time to time."

The spokesman would not comment on a suggestion in The Financial Times that the liquidation of some of its assets would be a way to generate cash to acquire a controlling stake in CIC, the state-owned bank being privatised.
Societe Generale is believed to have offered some six billion francs for a 67 percent stake in the bank, owned by French state-owned insurer GAN

At the end of August, Societe Generale had 54.3 billion francs in shareholders' equity, the spokesman said. Its equity portfolio had a book value of 21.7 billion francs and a market value of 24.6 billion. In addition, it had 12.3 billion francs in property assets.
The bank realised 600 million francs in capital gains on asset sales in the first half.
The bank started building up its asset portfolio in 1987, after its privatisation, and the portfolio was now "coming to its maturity", the spokesman said.
The newspaper report said that the asset sales could total about a third of the value of the portfolio.

While some French banks, such as Credit Lyonnais have suffered significant losses on their equity stakes, Societe Generale's portfolio has proved to be profitable, generating between 500 million and 800 million francs in profits each year.
The Financial Times said that there had been some suggestions from U.S. and North American investors that the bank's property and equity portfolio was too large for a bank.
